query: Why did secrets remain readable after removing access?
evidence: The service cached group membership in long-lived credentials. Short token lifetimes and a server-side revocation check bounded stale authorization.

query: How did we stop occasional garbled characters at chunk boundaries?
evidence: UTF-8 code points can span network packets. Keeping an incremental text decoder across reads prevented replacement characters when a multibyte sequence arrived in two pieces.

query: What solved the missing newest records when navigating results?
evidence: Offset pagination skipped rows when concurrent inserts shifted the list. A stable keyset cursor based on timestamp and unique identifier preserved traversal order.

query: Why did the monitor repeatedly restart a healthy but busy process?
evidence: A liveness probe shared the saturated request worker pool. Separating liveness from readiness prevented overload from becoming a restart storm.

query: How did we keep a wrong clock from expiring leases early?
evidence: Wall-clock corrections changed elapsed-duration calculations. Using a monotonic clock for lease intervals prevented clock synchronization from changing their duration.

query: What made the first request after an idle period so slow?
evidence: An aggressive idle timeout closed the upstream connection pool. Keeping a small warm connection pool removed repeated DNS lookup and TLS negotiation from the first request.
ERR_SYNC_701 meant the upload cursor referenced a retired generation. Refreshing the generation receipt before retrying fixed this error; changing the credentials did not.
ERR_SYNC_702 meant the remote device credential had expired. Issuing a replacement device token fixed this error; refreshing the generation receipt did not.
The reverse proxy stripped the /v2 prefix before forwarding /v2/export. Preserving the complete request path fixed the 404 response.
The /v2/import handler was excluded from the minimal build profile. Enabling the import feature at build time fixed its 404 response.
Commit ab41c92 made tombstone writes idempotent so a replayed deletion could not advance the publication counter twice.
Commit ab41c93 added explicit bounds to context expansion so requests spanning too many events returned a clear narrowing instruction.
